title: POC scoping - Nova Insurance - POC timeline and milestones
next_steps: Redwood to share POC statement of work and pricing by 2026-03-29
Customer to provide sample workload and S3 access by 2026-04-02
SE to run baseline latency/cost benchmark on sample set by 2026-04-10
action_items: Maya: Share sample datasets + infra diagram (due 2026-04-02)
Carlos: Provision benchmark harness and initial scripts (due 2026-04-09)
Ravi: Confirm SOC2/SAML requirements and provide contacts for compliance review (due 2026-04-01)
summary: AE+SE run through POC success criteria, workload sizing, and a proposed timeline of kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, and exec readout. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs hosted and has strict security requirements (VPC, KMS, audit logs). Agreed next steps: SOW/pricing, sample data access, kickoff on 2026-04-06, and initial benchmarks to follow.
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samantha, account exec on the Redwood side. We'll do intros quick and then jump into POC scope and timeline.
[00:08] Tom Alvarez: Hey Sam, Tom here. Maya, Ravi, Leah with me. Thanks.
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: Carlos, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll be running the benchmarks and setting up the POC infra with you.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Maya, platform eng, I'll coordinate infra and data access.
[00:21] Leah Gomez: Leah from product — I'll own success criteria from our side.
[00:24] Samantha Lee: Great. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, size the workload, agree benchmarks, then map to timeline and milestones — kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review, exec readout. 
[00:36] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. High level — Nova is evaluating for automated claims triage and policy Q&A. Our throughput during peak is about 120 reqs/min with ~30 tokens avg, but we also have some long-context cases ~1k tokens. Latency target is sub 400ms p95 for the short flows, cost is also a factor.
[01:00] Leah Gomez: Success criteria from product: 1) accuracy within existing model baseline (we'll share evals), 2) latency p95 under 400ms for short queries, 3) cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll attach target), 4) easy integration with our platform and auditability for compliance.
[01:18] Carlos Mendes: Helpful. For the POC we usually define success as hitting latency/cost/quality thresholds on the sample set and proving access/observability. We'll propose a 4–6 week POC with clear milestones.
[01:30] Ravi Patel: Security is key for us. We require data-in-transit and at-rest encryption, KMS integration, SAML SSO, and audit logs. On-prem options are interesting but prefer a VPC-connected private deployment if possible. Also, retention rules: logs kept x days and we need ability to purge.
[01:52] Samantha Lee: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; we can provide audit logs and configurable retention. We'll include SOC2 docs and our security packet in the SOW.
[02:05] Maya Chen: For infra, we need a checklist: network peering, service accounts, S3 bucket for sample data, and IAM roles. We can provision a test VPC.
[02:15] Carlos Mendes: I'll put together a detailed access checklist. For the benchmark harness, what sample size do you want? We typically run 1k short queries and 200 long-context queries to capture tail behavior.
[02:26] Tom Alvarez: That sounds reasonable. I'll aim to share a representative sample of ~1,200 queries and a small labeled eval set for quality checks.
[02:33] Samantha Lee: Great. So proposed milestone list: Kickoff (week 0) — project alignment and access handoff; Access/setup (week 1) — VPC peering, S3 access, creds; Baseline benchmarks (week 2) — run hosted baseline and Amber (dedicated) run if applicable; Mid-point review (week 3) — present initial latency/cost/quality and iterate; Final validation and exec readout (week 4–6) — present results, recommend config and next steps.
[03:00] Leah Gomez: Who typically owns the benchmark scripts?
[03:04] Carlos Mendes: Redwood will supply the harness and scripts; customer provides data and any special prompts. We can run locally in your VPC or from Redwood-managed infra depending on the deployment.
[03:15] Maya Chen: We'll prefer running within our VPC to verify network egress and latency; can Redwood run the harness from a bastion in our VPC?
[03:24] Carlos Mendes: Yep — we can deploy a small runner in your environment. We'll need an IAM role and an outbound egress rule for the runner to talk to the model endpoints if using hosted; if private deployment, the runner can talk locally.
[03:37] Tom Alvarez: On model variants — we're looking at a couple open models and maybe Redwood-verified versions. Cost/latency trade-offs are big. We might prefer quantized/or smaller models if quality holds.
[03:50] Samantha Lee: We'll make recommendations in the SOW: hosted vs dedicated vs private with expected p95 latencies and cost bands.
[03:58] Ravi Patel: A quick question on data residency — some claims data can't leave region. Can you host in our EU region?
[04:05] Carlos Mendes: Yes, we have region-located deployments. For Private we can deploy into your region/VPC. We'll note region in the SOW.
[04:13] Maya Chen: For the SSO flow — we'll need SAML integration for the console and RBAC. What's the lead time?
[04:19] Samantha Lee: SAML generally takes 1–2 weeks to configure once you share metadata. For the POC we can use temporary accounts if that's faster, but we'll prioritize SSO for production readiness.
[04:30] Leah Gomez: Let's talk acceptance tests — what do you measure for quality?
[04:33] Carlos Mendes: We'll run your labeled eval set and compute precision/recall and an aggregation metric to compare to baseline. We'll also do human spot checks on a sample. For latency, p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. For cost, cost per 1k tokens and per-inference.
[04:48] Tom Alvarez: Our legal asked about data deletion after POC and proof we didn't retain PII.
[04:52] Samantha Lee: We'll include a data handling appendix in the SOW and can provide logs showing deletes. Redwood Private gives you control over storage and we can sign data protection clauses.
[04:59] Maya Chen: Timeline — you mentioned kickoff 2026-04-06? That works for us.
[05:04] Samantha Lee: Yes, propose Tue 6th April at 9am PT for kickoff. If that works I'll lock it.
[05:09] Tom Alvarez: Works.
[05:11] Carlos Mendes: On benchmarks — quick technical note: short queries will be batched lightly to meet latency SLOs; long context tests will measure KV cache effectiveness. We'll also run a quality regression harness.
[05:23] Leah Gomez: For reporting, can we get per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns?
[05:27] Samantha Lee: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, traces, and cost breakdowns; we'll share screenshots in the kickoff.
[05:34] Ravi Patel: Any external audit or third-party pen test reports we can see?
[05:38] Samantha Lee: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and recent pentest summary in the security packet.
[05:43] Maya Chen: For POC duration, if we get everything setup quickly, can we compress to 3 weeks?
[05:48] Carlos Mendes: Possibly — baseline and mid-point checks can be compressed, but exec readout may need extra time for remediation. We'll propose a 4-week plan with optional compression if access is immediate.
[05:58] Tom Alvarez: Cost model for POC — are there credits or trial infra?
[06:02] Samantha Lee: We can provide limited credits for hosted runs and a discounted rate for dedicated infra during the POC. Details will be in the SOW.
[06:10] Leah Gomez: Ok, recap of success criteria from our side so it's explicit: meet or exceed baseline quality on labeled set, p95 latency <400ms for short queries, cost per 1k tokens below internal threshold, and audit/SSO/KMS compliance validated.
[06:26] Samantha Lee: Perfect. We'll include those as acceptance criteria in the SOW.
[06:31] Carlos Mendes: Next, quick checklist for access/setup: 1) sample S3 location and signed role, 2) VPC peering or site-to-site with runner, 3) SAML metadata if you want SSO for console, 4) contact for compliance.
[06:45] Maya Chen: I'll share S3 + infra diagram by Fri 2026-04-02.
[06:50] Samantha Lee: I'll send the SOW and pricing by Mon 2026-03-29. Carlos will share benchmark harness and runner instructions.
[06:58] Tom Alvarez: Any blockers from our side — legal wants to review the security packet before kickoff. Is that possible?
[07:04] Samantha Lee: Yes, we'll attach it with the SOW.
[07:07] Leah Gomez: Timeline and milestones — can you repeat proposed dates so we have them captured?
[07:11] Samantha Lee: Sure: Kickoff 2026-04-06; Access/setup complete by 2026-04-13; Baseline benchmarks 2026-04-14 to 2026-04-16; Mid-point review 2026-04-20; Final validation and exec readout week of 2026-04-27 (could extend to 2026-05-06 depending on remediation).
[07:33] Ravi Patel: We'll block those dates and I'll coordinate with legal for the security review.
[07:37] Carlos Mendes: One more technical note — for measuring cost we need realistic tokenization. Please let us know if you do any prompt engineering server-side or concatenation patterns.
[07:47] Tom Alvarez: We'll document prompt patterns and send them along.
[07:50] Samantha Lee: OK seems like alignment. Any final questions?
[07:55] Leah Gomez: None from product.
[07:57] Maya Chen: No, thanks.
[07:59] Samantha Lee: Thanks everyone — recap in writing and I'll follow up with SOW and security packet. Meeting adjourned.
[08:06] End of recording.
